items.title: Frank Chace Interview, 1961-11-18
items.q: John and I were talking earlier about who influenced Goodman and Lennon about Goodman's early playing.

ctx.x: Yeah. Fudd and Benny Goodman were together a little while in the Pollock Band. Do you think that there was a point of contact?

Yeah. Now, Goodman's something else. I don't know who influenced him. I don't mean to say it that way, but it's very difficult. John and I were talking earlier about who influenced Goodman and Lennon about Goodman's early playing. It was crackling hot and fleet and beautifully executed. But we can't, we can't decide where he got it from. I think, certainly on two separate occasions, on one, I think the record is After a While with Wingy Minow. I think it was on OK, reissued Columbia. Correct me if I'm wrong, he…

Well, I wondered whether Benny might have been influenced by some of the colored fellows. He didn't speak about influences from Rapolo. Rapolo was with the New Orleans Rhythm Kings when Benny was learning the clarinet. And they might even have traveled on the lake boats together. Because the New Orleans Rhythm Kings frequently rowed as guests across the lake in bands that Benny was playing with.
